subject: Issues compiling simple model for custom exponential (user guide example)

messages.author: ad91bbac71425e94
messages.subject: Issues compiling simple model for custom exponential (user guide example)
parts:
Hello all,
I've just stated using Stan, and I have been running through some examples in the Stan user guide. In the user guide, it indicates that a custom probability function can be made. The second example (pg 115) is to replace

x ~ exponential(lambda);

with

lp__ <- lp__ + log(lambda) - y * lambda;

However, when I try this, I get the following error:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'simpleex3' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=12, column=44

        lp__ <- lp__ + log(lambda) - x * lambda;
                                           ^-- here

Everything runs fine if I use the standard exponential function, but not the custom one. I imagine I'm missing something rather simple - could someone help me understand what the issue is?  R code, model, and error message attached.

Thanks in advance,
Ryan

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Issues compiling simple model for custom exponential (user guide example)
parts:
Hi Ryan,

If you read the error message, it states:

    DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
    no matches for function name="multiply"
        arg 0 type=real[1]

This is trying to let you know that multiplication isn't vectorized. That is, the first argument, x, can't be an array. (x is defined as "real x[N]", which is showing up as "type=real[1]" in the parser.)


The fix is simple. Replace the single, vectorized call with a loop. The original line:

The fixed lines:

    for (n in 1:N) {
      lp__ <- lp__ + log(lambda) - x[n] * lambda;
    }



Daniel


PS. The files were attached, but Bob's email program may have eaten them.

parts:
The problem is that "*" is mapped to the
function "multiply" internally, but we haven't
mapped the error functions back. Bad form on our
part --- we'll get around to that eventually.

- Bob
